text:
Alex Moore: hey team, seeing a sustained throughput drop across several p99 paths since ~00:05 UTC, looks correlated with repeated worker restarts :alarm_clock:
Priya Shah: saw that, p50 fine but p99 latency + retries up. Any obvious OOM logs?
Mateo Rivera: yep, grep shows a flurry of `cudaMalloc` failures on worker-37 and worker-42 around 00:07. sample: `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory when allocating 1.2 GiB`
Jin Park: also see kernel switch to fallback path in logs: `kernel_selector: switched to generic_attention_v1 for model v2.3` right before restart spikes
Ops Lucy: SRE Bot reported autoscaler thrash and then restarted the pool: @deploy-bot rolled back a kernel rollout at 00:10 :arrow_backward:
SRE Bot: incident created INC-2026-0318-18, linked perf profile snapshot `snap-20260318-a1`
Alex Moore: KV cache eviction rate spiked too, eviction/sec went from ~30 -> ~750 within 5m. suspect fragmentation causing allocator failures and then OOMs
Priya Shah: interesting — batching heuristic also toggled to `min_batch` mode per logs, so tail latency worsened while throughput dropped
Mateo Rivera: attaching short perf dump snippet: 
```
PID 3721 worker-37: alloc failed at 0x7f8b3c000 size 128M
kernel: generic_attention_v1 selected (fallback); latency jumped +22ms
kv_cache: slab_free went down 40% -> compaction triggered
```
Jin Park: flamegraph link from snap: https://perf.redwood/snap-20260318-a1/flame.html (top frames show allocator::alloc and kv_cache::evict)
Ops Lucy: who's owning hotfix? Can we pin kernel_selector to previous stable for affected pools and bump prefetch threshold?
Alex Moore: I'll pin kernel selection for the q4-serving pool to `fast_attention_v4` for rollout id r-2026-03-18-01 and keep traffic on fallback zeroed. also increasing kv prefetch threshold by +8MB to reduce sweep frequency
Priya Shah: quick mitigation: reduce max_batch_size to 8 for p99-sensitive routes (should reduce transient mem spikes)
Mateo Rivera: ran quick sim on staging; lowering batch size avoids immediate cudaMalloc failures but throughput drops ~12% — acceptable as short-term mitigation
Jin Park: noted a regression in kernel heuristics from last week change: commit 58b9d7 altered decision threshold from 0.6 -> 0.4, making selector prefer generic kernel earlier. Likely root contributor
SRE Bot: deploy-bot: rollback completed for rollout r-2026-03-17-ker-heuristic (status: success) :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: new rollout r-2026-03-18-01 pinned to fast_attention_v4 (status: in_progress)
Ops Lucy: monitoring dashboards — KV eviction back down to ~45/sec, worker restarts stopped after 00:13 UTC :relieved:
Alex Moore: postmortem action items: 1) revert kernel heuristic change in mainline 2) add circuit-breaker to prevent kernel rollouts if eviction/sec > 200 3) add allocator entropy metric to alerting 4) long-term: compaction improvements and better slab packing
Priya Shah: I'll own item 2 and 3, adding alert thresholds and runbook
Mateo Rivera: I'll draft a short regression test for kernel-selector that simulates fragmented KV and small-batch bursts
Jin Park: add perf regression gate to CI that runs `snap-20260318` profile as baseline
Ops Lucy: thanks team — keeping this thread for updates, will open follow-up with timeline and customer impact once we have full metrics
Alex Moore: timeline note: incident start ~2425001111, mitigations in place by 2425001210, stabilised by 2425001300. will record final numbers in postmortem
Priya Shah: thanks all, leaving logs and flamegraphs in the incident folder: s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-0318-18/
SRE Bot: incident INC-2026-0318-18 status: mitigated (monitoring)
Alex Moore: :thumbsup: closing thread after postmortem doc is uploaded
